title: A perfect complex is pseudo-coherent with locally finite Tor dimension
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $E$ be a perfect object of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex]. Then $E$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], and $E$ locally has finite Tor dimension: every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with integers $a\le b$ such that $H^i(E|_U\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_U}\mathcal G)=0$ for every $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal G$ and every $i\notin[a,b]$.

proof.text: At each point unpack perfectness [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Apply [lem-pc-strictly-perfect-finite-free-refinement] to the chosen strictly perfect local model. This gives a smaller neighbourhood and a bounded finite-free complex representing the restriction. Forget its lower bound to obtain the bounded-above finite-free model in [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex].

For the Tor clause use the same finite-free refinement. Transport the complex through Modules.overEquiv U. The equivalence preserves zero objects and coproducts and identifies the unit with the unit of U.toScheme, so the transported complex has the same termwise bounds and finite-free terms. Finite free terms are flat: use [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] and the Grothendieck abelian structure, apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coproduct] to a finite coproduct of units, and transport exactness along the term isomorphisms. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat] to obtain a K-flat representative.

The private open_model_iso proves that the transported representative represents derivedPullback U.ι of E: tensorPullback is isomorphic to ordinary open restriction by uniqueness of left adjoints; exact open restriction composed with the over-site equivalence induces mapDerivedCategory. The universal property in [def-pc-derived-pullback] and leftDerivedUnique identify its derived functor with this exact restriction. Compose mapDerivedCategoryNatIso, mapDerivedCategoryCompIso, the given model isomorphism, and mapDerivedCategoryFactors.

For any module G and degree n outside [min a b,b], n is outside [a,b], so the transported representative P has zero term in degree n. mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso identifies P tensor G[0] with termwise tensorRight G applied to P. Tensor preserves zero objects; the short-complex lemma isZero_homology_of_isZero_X₂ gives zero homology in degree n. P, its K-flatness, and the inverse representing isomorphism are the witnesses in [def-pc-derived-tensor-cohomology-vanishes]. Since min a b ≤ b and the bounds are independent of G, unpacking [def-pc-locally-finite-tor-dimension] concludes.

split_report.summary: Checked the item against Stacks Cohomology Lemma 08CQ, implication (1) => (2). The proof now has two steps: a strictly perfect local model is bounded-above finite free, hence pseudo-coherent; and its bounded flat tensor model is K-flat and bounded, giving a local finite Tor interval. No child node was created because the first step is elementary from the definitions and the second uses the existing K-flat lemma.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the affine perfectness proof clause invoking the forward implication of Stacks Tag 08CQ: a perfect complex is pseudo-coherent and locally of finite Tor dimension.

tool_uses.why: The affine strictly perfect model has finite projective terms; this existing module lemma supplies the finite principal-open refinement needed to meet the finite-free local formulation of pseudo-coherence.

The proof needs the generic K-flatness theorem for bounded-above flat complexes to identify derived tensor with the ordinary tensor model; that theorem belongs to the semicontinuity unit and is not restated in this Picard unit.
